```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Global chunk options control how code and output appear in the HTML file.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  comment = NA,
  fig.width = 4.5,
  fig.height = 3.2,
  out.width = "50%"
)
```

# Aim

In this exercise you will complete a short RMarkdown report and render it to HTML.

Replace each `___` blank with the correct code or text. The document will not render until all blanks are completed.

This report should demonstrate:

- section headings,
- R code chunks and simple chunk options such as `echo`,
- inline R code,
- loading packages and data,
- rendering a table and a figure,
- cross-referencing a table and a figure,
- citing a source from a `.bib` file.

The data used in this exercise come from a study on reaction time and ageing using the Nintendo Wii Balance Board by Blomkvist and colleagues. Cite the paper here using the existing BibTeX entry in `references.bib`: `___`.

# Optional Citation Practice

Complete this extension task after your report renders successfully.

Add this reaction-time methods article to the report.

APA reference to turn into a BibTeX entry:

Whelan, R. (2008). Effective analysis of reaction time data. *The Psychological Record, 58*, 475-482. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF03395630

1. Open `references.bib`.
2. Add a BibTeX entry for the Whelan article at the end of the file. You can get the entry from Google Scholar or ask ChatGPT/Copilot to create one from the APA reference above.
3. Use a clear citation key, for example `whelan2008reactiontime`.
4. Replace the comment below with one sentence that cites the article using `@whelan2008reactiontime`.
5. Render again and check that the citation appears in the text and in the reference list.
